root_cause.text: The `ocfs2_group_extend` function in the OCFS2 subsystem incorrectly assumes that the global bitmap inode block is always valid, triggering a kernel panic via `BUG_ON` when encountering an invalid dinode that bypassed structural validation through JBD2-managed buffer paths.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `BUG_ON(!OCFS2_IS_VALID_DINODE(fe))` in `fs/ocfs2/resize.c` with an explicit validation check and error handling (`ocfs2_error`) to handle invalid dinodes gracefully instead of crashing the kernel.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerability by replacing a safe error-handling check (which returned -EIO and went to out_unlock) with a panic-inducing BUG_ON() statement. Specifically, it removes the check on lines 322-326 and adds 'BUG_ON(!OCFS2_IS_VALID_DINODE(fe));' on line 319. This causes a kernel panic when encountering an invalid dinode instead of handling it gracefully.
